title: Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, alerts and Application Insights
learningObjective: Describe Azure Monitor, including Log Analytics, Azure Monitor alerts and Application Insights.
foundation: Azure Monitor collects data about your resources and apps (in Azure, on-premises and other clouds), analyses it and helps you act on it.
Two main data types: metrics (numbers over time, like CPU %) and logs (records of events, like errors or sign-ins).
Log Analytics is where you query logs. Alerts tell you when something needs attention. Application Insights watches your web apps: requests, failures, response times.
engineer: Data sources: application, operating system (with the Azure Monitor Agent and data collection rules), Azure resources (platform metrics collected automatically; resource logs via diagnostic settings), subscription (Activity log: who did what, when) and tenant (Entra ID logs). Custom sources via APIs.

Metrics: lightweight, near real-time, stored in a time-series database; view in Metrics explorer. Logs: stored in a Log Analytics workspace; query with Kusto Query Language (KQL) in Log Analytics; e.g. Heartbeat | summarize count() by Computer.

Azure Monitor alerts: alert rules evaluate metrics (metric alerts), log queries (log search alerts) or the Activity log (activity log alerts, including Service Health); when triggered they call action groups (email, SMS, push, voice, webhook, Logic App, Function, ITSM). Alert processing rules can suppress or route alerts.

Application Insights: application performance monitoring (APM) for web apps on Azure, on-premises or other clouds. Enable with auto-instrumentation or an SDK (OpenTelemetry). Tracks request rates, response times, failure rates, dependency calls, exceptions, page views, user and session counts, and performance counters; availability tests ping your endpoints. Workspace-based, stored in Log Analytics.
Visualise and act: dashboards, workbooks, Power BI, Grafana; autoscale and automated responses from alerts.

example.title: An online bank's monitoring
body: Platform metrics show database DTU; a metric alert emails DBAs when it stays above 90%. The Azure Monitor Agent sends VM security event logs to a Log Analytics workspace, where a log search alert flags repeated failed sign-ins.
Application Insights shows that the payment page's response time doubled after a release and pinpoints a slow dependency call.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription (a free account works)
permissions: Reader to explore; Contributor to create resources
limits: Log ingestion and retention beyond included amounts are billed
portal: Monitor > Metrics; Monitor > Logs (KQL); Monitor > Alerts > Create alert rule; Monitor > Action groups.
Resource > Diagnostic settings: send resource logs to a workspace.
Create a resource > Application Insights; or App Service > Application Insights > Turn on.
configuration.cli:
az monitor metrics list --resource <vm-id> --metric "Percentage CPU" --interval PT5M
az monitor log-analytics query -w <workspace-guid> --analytics-query "Heartbeat | summarize count() by Computer"
az monitor action-group create -g <rg> -n oncall --short-name oncall --action email ops ops@contoso.com

troubleshooting.symptom: Log query returns no data from a VM.
troubleshooting.cause: No Azure Monitor Agent or data collection rule.
troubleshooting.fix: Install the agent and associate a DCR with the VM.

troubleshooting.symptom: Alert fires but nobody is told.
troubleshooting.cause: No action group on the rule.

comparisons.difference: Metrics: numeric, fast, near real-time. Logs: rich records, queried with KQL.
App Insights collects app telemetry; Log Analytics is the query tool and workspace store.
Monitor: your resources; Service Health: the Azure platform.

misconceptions.myth: Azure Monitor only works for Azure resources.
misconceptions.reality: It also monitors on-premises and other clouds.
It supports many languages via OpenTelemetry.
Resource logs need diagnostic settings; OS logs need the agent.

architectureDecisions: Send resource logs to a central workspace.
Use metric alerts for fast numeric signals; log alerts for patterns.
Enable Application Insights for every web app.
